content:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts observed for private-inference-gateway in eu-west-1. Error rate spike ~18% vs baseline. Paging oncall: @oncall-amber :rotating_light:
oncall-amber: I'm on it. grabbing logs and checking the runbook now. pinging infra team.

oncall-amber: Quick snapshot from the APIGW metrics — 502/504 surge starts ~3132104200 and correlates with increased SYN retransmits toward 10.0.58.0/24 (private inference nodes).
sandeep: I see a pattern in the NAT metrics: ephemeral port usage across the transit NATs is at 98% on gateway-az-a. Could be port depletion but logs also show a lot of TCP RSTs.

maria: running tcpdump on a healthy vs failing path. failing path shows continuous TCP RSTs from 10.0.2.5 -> 172.31.200.40 after the TLS handshake completes. healthy path does not.

jordan: curious — did we roll any security group or peering changes? I remember a small SG egress tighten that went out in eu-west-1 last night. liz: yeah, we shipped SG rollout: restrict ephemeral egress to only transit-proxies (rule id sg-rl-2026). That was to lock down accidental egress to legacy gateways.

oncall-amber: timeline: SG rollout 02:10 UTC, errors up ~02:20 UTC, error spike steady. This looks suspicious.

infra-bot: Deploy log: sg-rl-2026 rolled to 85% of eu-west-1 private subnets at 3132104100 by infra-canary.
sandeep: The SG rule is denying ephemeral ports from inference nodes to the NAT/peering appliance IP range. That explains the RSTs when the appliance tries to send back ephemeral replies — asymmetric flow.

maria: repro test: from control-plane shell -> curl to private inference endpoint returns 504. tcpdump on node shows SYN-ACK arrives, then node sends RST — because connection track doesn't see flow? full snippet:
```
16:21:03.123456 IP 172.31.200.40.53218 > 10.0.2.5.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
16:21:03.124678 IP 10.0.2.5.443 > 172.31.200.40.53218: Flags [S.], seq 54321, ack 12346, win 28960, length 0
16:21:03.124700 IP 172.31.200.40.53218 > 10.0.2.5.443: Flags [R], seq 12346, win 0, length 0
```

jordan: Confirmed: SG denies return path on ephemeral ports. This breaks NAT/passthrough patterns for the inference gateway.

oncall-amber: Mitigation option A: rollback sg-rl-2026 to 0% for eu-west-1 (fast). Option B: add explicit allow for transit appliance CIDR to ephemeral ports on SG (safer). Which do we prefer?

sandeep: Add allow for transit appliance ephemeral range is minimally invasive and fast — but rollout may still take ~3-5m to propagate. Rollback is instant once we push revert.

oncall-amber: I'm going to open a revert to be fastest and then create a targeted allow so we can reapply secure posture. kicking off revert now. @infra-bot run revert sg-rl-2026 eu-west-1

infra-bot: Revert job started. Estimated completion ~45s. Job id: infra-job-98342.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigation in progress — revert sg-rl-2026. Postmortem checklist item created in incidents tracker.

maria: just captured visible improvement: error rate dropping from 18% -> 3% in last 60s. tcpdump shows no immediate RSTs on the calls that were failing.

oncall-amber: passing to secondary SRE for post-mitigation validation and long-term fix. @jordan please pick this up for follow-up (root cause, why SG rollout targeted wrong CIDR, and better canary signals).

jordan: taking. I'll coordinate with security to author targeted allow rule and re-run rollout with stricter canary gating. also will add a test that verifies symmetric flows with transit appliance as part of rollout gate.

customer-success-beth: CS update: We have 4 paying customers that hit increased latency/errors in the last 10 minutes. I'm drafting a short note: apology, what happened, steps we took to mitigate, and ETA for full RCA. Will coordinate with SRE and legal if needed.

oncall-amber: thanks Beth. Action items: 1) Jordan owns RCA and remediation (include runbook updates) 2) Sandeep to validate NAT capacity and add ephemeral port headroom 3) Maria to publish packet snippets and timeline to incident ticket 4) Amber to close paging after 30m of stable metrics.

jordan: Initial root cause: overly-broad SG egress tighten blocked ephemeral return traffic to transit appliance IPs — caused asymmetric TCP and RSTs leading to gateway 5xx/timeouts. Secondary contributing factor: NAT ephemeral pool near capacity amplified failures for existing flows.

sandeep: I'll provision additional NAT ports and schedule a quota bump. Also will add alert for ephemeral utilization > 75% per NAT instance.

oncall-amber: closing the paging in 30m if errors remain low. final note for postmortem: verify rollout automation prevents lockouts to critical infra.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated (partial) — status requires RCA. Marking as "under investigation".

customer-success-beth: final to CS: sent initial customer note to affected accounts. linking to incident ticket and ETA for RCA (24-48h).

liz: small ops note — if anyone needs to reproduce locally, use this quick check:
```
# from a test host in the private subnet
nc -vz -w 3 10.0.2.5 443 || echo "conn fail"
# check conntrack for ephemeral entries
sudo conntrack -L | grep 10.0.2.5
```

oncall-amber: thanks all. handing off to Jordan for RCA. I am un-paged. :white_check_mark:"
